// diagnostic

E-ERR-DEFAULT

`!` is a retired bare default failure contract.

What

`!` is a retired bare default failure contract.

Why

Ordinary fallible functions use the implicit default `Err` contract; the `!` prefix is only for a named error domain.

Fix

remove `!`; failure is implicit, or name an explicit domain such as `!IOError`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E-ERR-DEFAULT: tests/ui/retired_void_result.stderr.

Error [E0431]: `Void` is retired
  --> tests/ui/retired_void_result.jet:1:13
    |
  1 | fn run() => Void ! {
    |             ^^^^
 Why: Jet uses `()` for a result with no information; non-returning paths are compiler facts under D-NEVER1
 Fix: Replace `Void` with `()`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0431

Error [E0068]: This callable uses the retired result-arrow shape.
  --> tests/ui/retired_void_result.jet:1:10
    |
  1 | fn run() => Void ! {
    |          ^^
 Why: A return type sits after the parameter list, and `->` introduces the body; an effect ceiling follows the return type
 Fix: Write `fn name(...) Type -> body`, or `fn name(...) Type -[Effects]> { … }`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0068

Error [E0003]: This unit-fallible signature uses the retired arrow-and-unit form
  --> tests/ui/retired_void_result.jet:1:13
    |
  1 | fn run() => Void ! {
    |             ^^^^^^
 Why: A function that can fail but returns no value has no result payload for an arrow to introduce
 Fix: Write `fn save(path: String) !IOError`, or omit the contract for implicit `Err`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0003
